sections.name: companyProjects
sections.title: Loading company fields for every project
sections.what: Reads the id, industry, operator and parties of all projects in one query. The company search uses this list.
sections.why: Likely reason: the search needs every project to scan company names.
sections.watch_out: The whole projects table is read on each call, so this will slow as the table grows.

summary: Works out which companies own, operate or develop each project, so the app can search projects by company.
purpose: Gives the company search a list of company names per project and a matching key.
why: The code comment says suppliers and EPC contractors do not imply ownership, so only owner-type roles count. Likely reason: keeps company search results accurate.
how: 1. Read each project's id, industry, operator name and list of parties. 2. Collect the operator name plus any party whose role is owner, operator, developer, sponsor, joint venture or JV partner, ignoring capital letters. 3. Remove blank names and duplicates, and trim spaces. 4. Provide a lowercase key so names match regardless of capitalization.
inputs: Rows from the projects table holding the operator field and the parties field.
outputs: A list of company names for each project, a lowercase matching key, and the project rows with company fields.
risks: Only the exact listed role words count. A role such as owner-operator or a different spelling is silently ignored. The company list is read from the whole projects table each time.
debug: If a company is missing from search, check that the project's operator field or its party role is one of the listed words, and check the spelling of the company name.
